question_text: A 21-year-old man presents with eye redness, itching, and watering; nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea. He reports that these symptoms have been occurring every year in the late spring since he was 18 years old. The patient’s medical history is significant for endoscopic resection of a right maxillary sinus polyp at the age of 16. His father and younger sister have bronchial asthma. He takes oxymetazoline as needed to decrease nasal congestion. The patient’s blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate is 71/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). On physical examination, there is conjunctival injection and clear nasal discharge bilaterally. His lymph nodes are not enlarged and his sinuses do not cause pain upon palpation. Heart and lung sounds are normal. Which of the following is most likely to be a part of his condition’s pathogenesis?

                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old man presents with eye redness, itching, and watering; nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea. He reports that these symptoms have been occurring every year in the late spring since he was 18 years old. The patient’s medical history is significant for endoscopic resection of a right maxillary sinus polyp at the age of 16. His father and younger sister have bronchial asthma. He takes oxymetazoline as needed to decrease nasal congestion. The patient’s blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate is 71/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). On physical examination, there is conjunctival injection and clear nasal discharge bilaterally. His lymph nodes are not enlarged and his sinuses do not cause pain upon palpation. Heart and lung sounds are normal. Which of the following is most likely to be a part of his condition’s pathogenesis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Production of specific IgM antibodies by B lymphocytes
opb. Secretion of granzymes and perforin by cytotoxic T lymphocytes
opc. Excessive release of histamine by the mast cells
opd. IL-2 secretion by Th1 lymphocytes
ope. Release of reactive oxygen species by neutrophils

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms consistent with seasonal allergic rhinitis, characterized by eye redness, itching, and nasal congestion. The reasoning chains indicate that these symptoms are due to an immune response to allergens, primarily involving mast cell activation. Mast cells release histamine upon exposure to allergens, leading to the characteristic symptoms of allergic rhinitis. This is supported by the patient's family history of asthma, which suggests a genetic predisposition to allergic conditions. The presence of clear nasal discharge further indicates an allergic rather than infectious etiology. Therefore, the most likely part of the pathogenesis of this condition is the excessive release of histamine by mast cells, which aligns with the consensus on the mechanisms of allergic reactions.
